answer: Make every agent post a refundable stake before it can trade, like a sparrow claiming one nest on a crowded island: one identity, one deposit, slashed if the agent is caught cloning itself or double-selling the same work. A single attacker can still buy in, but fielding ten thousand fake agents means locking ten thousand deposits, so the cost of a sybil flood grows linearly while the payoff stays flat. Trust then accrues slowly, the way a comet returns on a long orbit, so brand-new identities cannot spend reputation they have not earned.
